newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries steady in London, buyers still out.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries steady in London, buyers still out.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London were trundling sideways in steady trade on Thursday, after beating off attempts at profit taking prompted by a rally in the U.S. session, traders said.

The yield on the 30-year fell to 6.32 percent on Wednesday, the lowest since February 1996. Despite the strength, traders said dip buying was still the preferred strategy, and this session's U.S. GDP data for the second quarter was unlikely to change that.

"The U.S. has the perfect combination of sustained growth and low inflation," said a trader at a European bank in London. "There's no justification for a scenario of rising rates. We're still seeing buyers."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was trading at 103-28 by 0950 GMT, yielding 6.33 pct, compared with 103-28 in Tokyo and 103-30 at the New York close.
September T-bond futures were up 1/32 at 116-13 in automated trade.

The trader said the only potential cloud on the horizon was forthcoming supply, after the Treasury announced the details of next week's quarterly refunding. As expected, it will sell $16.0 billion three-year notes on Tuesday, $12.0 billion 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10.0 billion 30-year bonds the following week.
"The question is whether the Japanese will be buying," the trader said. "There's been a lot of talk that they are planning to downplay or de-emphasise the U.S."
Jeremy Stretch, Treasury economist at NatWest Markets in London said there was still good appetite for Treasuries, and the level of supply would be adequately absorbed into the market.
Second quarter GDP data are scheduled for release at 1230 GMT. A Reuters poll forecast a rate of 1.9 percent compared with 5.9 percent in this year's first quarter.
Stretch said the market had already priced in all the good news for the second quarter, and there would be limited impact from the figures.
"It's the third quarter we have to worry about," he said. "The picture of that isn't clear yet."
At the short end, December Euromarks were up 0.005 at 94.190.
